title: GRID_ALPHA=46 claims '18% — map.odin grid blend' but the live canon blends 9% (view.odin LEFOU pass)
evidence: tools/render_dublin_preview.py:33: `GRID_ALPHA = 46       # 18% of 255 — map.odin grid blend` (docstring L9 repeats "grid (18% blend)", L102 "# --- grid (18% blend over land AND water — map.odin) ---"). app/render/view.odin:528-536 (read at the reviewed tree): `// v2-look-polish evening pass (LEFOU): the grid was the second-loudest` / `// element on the frame ("reads as graph paper") — the MM whitespace cut` / `// halves the 7.1 blend again (18% → 9%): the snap lattice stays visible` / `// for placement, but the paper reads clean under the ribbons.` / `g, c := p.grid, p.canvas` / `grid_soft := rl.Color{` / `u8((u16(g.r)*9 + u16(c.r)*91) / 100),` / `u8((u16(g.g)*9 + u16(c.g)*91) / 100),` / `u8((u16(g.b)*9 + u16(c.b)*91) / 100), 255}`
detail: The game's map_draw blends 9% grid / 91% canvas; the preview draws grid at alpha 46/255 (18%) — 2× the canon strength — while claiming to mirror it. The cited blend also lives in view.odin map_draw, not map.odin.
recommended_fix: Set GRID_ALPHA = 23 (9% of 255) to match view.odin's grid_soft blend, and fix the comments/docstring to cite view.odin map_draw at 9%.

title: `if args.bake or True:` is always true — the --bake flag has no distinct behavior
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:574: `ap.add_argument("--bake", action="store_true", help="bake dublin.json from cache (fetch if missing)")` and 586-590: `if args.bake or True:` / `    fetch_raw(args.cache)  # cache-first: no network when present` / `    bake(args.cache, args.out)` / `    verify(args.out, args.cache)`
detail: `or True` makes the condition unconditional, so passing --bake is identical to passing no flag; the advertised flag is dead and the condition is misleading dead code.
recommended_fix: Drop `or True` (e.g. `if args.bake or not (args.fetch or args.verify):`) or remove the --bake flag and document the default path.

title: fetched_utc is derived from cache-file mtimes, so byte-identity of the verify gate depends on the filesystem, not content
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:506: `"fetched_utc": _fetch_time(cache_dir),` and 541-552: `def _fetch_time(cache_dir: str) -> str:` / `    base = cache_path(cache_dir)` / `    files = [f"{base}.{key}.json" for key, _ in _queries()]` / `    times = []` / `    for p in files:` / `        try:` / `            times.append(os.stat(p).st_mtime)` / `        except OSError:` / `            pass` / `    if not times:` / `        return "unknown"` / `    return datetime.fromtimestamp(max(times), tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")`
detail: The tool's contract is 'same cached raw response -> byte-identical dublin.json', but a touch/copy of the cache changes mtimes and breaks --verify despite identical content.
recommended_fix: Derive fetched_utc from the cached responses' own osm3s.timestamp_osm_base field (content-derived), or omit it from the hash-compared asset.

title: render_dublin_preview.py re-implements the bake's bbox→UTM→board fit math instead of importing it
evidence: tools/render_dublin_preview.py:180-190: `# Tile coords for crop anchors (same math as osm_extract.bake).` / `import pyproj` / `tr = pyproj.Transformer.from_crs("WGS84", "EPSG:32629", always_xy=True)` / `...` / `ox0 = cxm - (b["w_tiles"] / scale) / 2.0` / `utm_top = cym + (b["h_tiles"] / scale) / 2.0`. tools/osm_extract.py:354-368 (the original): `ul = transformer.transform(BBOX_W, BBOX_N)` / `lr = transformer.transform(BBOX_E, BBOX_S)` / `scale = min(BOARD_W_TILES / utm_w, BOARD_H_TILES / utm_h)  # tiles per meter` / `cxm = (utm_x0 + utm_x1) / 2.0` / `ox0 = cxm - (BOARD_W_TILES / scale) / 2.0` / `utm_top = cym + (BOARD_H_TILES / scale) / 2.0`
detail: Two hand-maintained copies of the projection fit; if the bake's fit changes, crop anchors silently drift out of sync with the asset.
recommended_fix: Import the fit from tools/osm_extract.py (same directory, e.g. a shared board_fit(bbox, board) helper) instead of restating the math.

title: Unused imports in osm_extract.py: `io` and shapely's `shape`
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:49: `import io`; :59: `from shapely.geometry import LineString, Point, Polygon, shape`. A grep for `\bio\.` and `shape(` over the whole file (593 lines, read at the reviewed tree bd394fc) returns 0 matches — neither name is used.
detail: Leftover imports from an earlier pipeline shape; they mislead readers about the tool's real dependencies (io, and shapely.shape for raw geojson).
recommended_fix: Delete `import io` and drop `shape` from the shapely.geometry import list.

title: MIN_AREA water comment '~220 m x 220 m' is ~3× off — that figure belongs to the park threshold
evidence: tools/osm_extract.py:164-168: `MIN_AREA = {` / `    "water": 0.01,   # ~220 m x 220 m at this scale — ponds read as dots` / `    "coast": 0.005,` / `    "park": 0.1,     # ~2 football fields — real parks only` / `}`. The committed asset data/maps/dublin.json board.scale_tiles_per_m = 0.0013971214, so 0.01 tile² = 5,123 m² = 71.6 m × 71.6 m; a ~226 m side corresponds to park's 0.1 tile².
detail: The comment misstates the water noise floor by ~9× in area (71.6 m side, not 220 m), misleading future tuning of the anti-noise thresholds.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment to '~70 m x 70 m' (or move the ~220 m figure to the park line where it is true).
